subject: A Level Chemistry
title: Boltzmann distribution at two temperatures
question:
Fig. 5.1 shows the Boltzmann distribution of molecular energies for a sample of gas at two temperatures, T₁ and T₂.
(a) State which temperature is higher. Explain your answer.
(b) Use Fig. 5.1 to explain why the rate of reaction increases with temperature.

scene: Both curves are calculated from the formula, so the hotter curve is lower, wider and further to the right, as it should be.
svg: Each curve is 201 points worked out by hand.

figure:
A Boltzmann distribution graph. The horizontal axis is labelled kinetic energy and the vertical axis number of molecules, with no numbers.
Two curves start at the origin.
T₁ is a solid curve with a tall, narrow peak.
T₂ is a dashed curve for the higher temperature. It has a lower peak, further to the right, and a longer tail above T₁ at high energies.
A vertical dashed line at the activation energy, labelled Ea, well to the right of both peaks.
Label the curves T₁ and T₂.
Caption: Fig. 5.1.
